t:
That 
    (a) section 1(c) of the Civil Service Retirement Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. 2251(c)), is amended by inserting “an officer or employee of the United States Botanic Garden,” immediately following “the Architect of the Capitol and the employees of the Architect of the Capitol,”. 
    (b) Section 2(c) of such Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. 2252(c)), is amended by inserting “and officers and employees of the United States Botanic Garden” immediately following “the employees of the Architect of the Capitol”. 
    (c) Section 2(f) of such Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. 2252(f)), is amended by striking out “; and the Architect of the Capitol and the Librarian of Congress are authorized to exclude from the operation of this Act any employees under the office of the Architect of the Capitol and the Library of Congress, respectively, whose tenure of employment is temporary or of uncertain duration.” and inserting in lieu thereof “; and the Architect of the Capitol, the Librarian of Congress, and the Director or Acting Director of the United States Botanic Garden are authorized to exclude from the operation of this Act any employees under the office of the Architect of the Capitol, the Library of Congress, and the United States Botanic Garden, respectively, whose tenure of employment is temporary or of uncertain duration.”.

fable.w: The section only amends the Civil Service Retirement Act to cover officers and employees of the United States Botanic Garden and lets federal officials exclude temporary employees. The tempting reading is that the authority to exclude employees is a decision involving others, but every actor here (the Architect of the Capitol, the Librarian of Congress, the Botanic Garden Director, federal employees) is inside the federal government. There is no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving outside parties.
fable.s: the Architect of the Capitol, the Librarian of Congress, and the Director or Acting Director of the United States Botanic Garden are authorized to exclude from the operation of this Act any employees

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Civil Service Retirement Act to include employees of the United States Botanic Garden in the retirement system. It deals with the administrative classification and benefits of federal employees. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or private organizations) in the decision-making process. The actors involved are all within the federal government.
qwen_block.s: section 1(c) of the Civil Service Retirement Act, as amended (5 U.S.C. 2251(c)), is amended by inserting “an officer or employee of the United States Botanic Garden,” immediately following “the Architect of the Capitol and the employees of the Architect of the Capitol,”.

The power to exclude employees looks like a decision process, but it stays entirely inside the government.

No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue.
